introduction: The Unified Terminal IO module (`agentfox/io/`) is a shared library imported by both the `af` and `spec` CLIs that consolidates all terminal output logic — including JSON serialization, error envelopes, spinner display, format dispatch, and common CLI flags — into a single, consistent implementation. It eliminates duplicated I/O code, establishes a unified error envelope schema, and provides an `AF_AGENT=1` environment variable toggle for agent-mode defaults across both tools.

glossary.AF_AGENT: Environment variable; when set to exactly `"1"`, activates agent mode by defaulting `json_mode=True` and `quiet=True` for the CLI session.
glossary.AgentError: Exception class from the `agentspec` package representing agent-layer errors; carries an optional `.category` attribute.
glossary.AgentFoxError: Base exception class in `agentfox/core/errors.py` from which all agentfox-specific errors inherit.
glossary.AgentFoxGroup: A Click Group subclass defined in `agentfox/io/cli.py` that handles banner rendering, error routing, and OutputManager construction for both CLIs.
glossary.AgentSpecError: Exception class from the `agentspec` package (subclass of `AgentError`) representing spec-processing errors.
glossary.AppTheme: Existing theme class in `agentfox/ui/display.py` whose `console` attribute is used by `StatusSpinner` for styled stderr output.
glossary.BannerGroup: Legacy Click group class in `af/app.py` that handled banner rendering and error handling; replaced by `AgentFoxGroup` in this spec.
glossary.BrokenPipeError: Python exception raised when writing to a closed pipe (e.g. when stdout consumer exits early); silently suppressed by all emit functions.
glossary.Hypothesis: Property-based testing library already used in this project, used for error envelope serialization property tests.
glossary.JSONL: JSON Lines format: one compact JSON object per line, no indentation, used by `emit_line`.
glossary.LiveAwareHandler: Existing log handler that routes Python log records through Rich Live, integrated with `StatusSpinner`.
glossary.OutputManager: Central coordinator class for all CLI output, constructed once at startup and stored in `ctx.obj["output"]`; controls json_mode, quiet, verbose, and trace settings.
glossary.PlanSpinner: Legacy spinner class in `agentfox/ui/progress.py`, superseded by the new unified `StatusSpinner` in this spec.
glossary.ProgressDisplay: Existing multi-task progress display class in `agentfox/ui/progress.py` for `af code` orchestration; not merged in this spec.
glossary.SessionError: Exception class from the `agentspec` package representing session-layer errors; always maps to `session_error` type with `retryable: false`.
glossary.StatusSpinner: The unified animated progress indicator class in `agentfox/io/spinner.py`, replacing both `PlanSpinner` and the old `StatusSpinner`.
glossary._json_explicit: Sentinel key written to `ctx.obj` by the `--json`/`--no-json` option callback when the user explicitly passes either flag, used to distinguish explicit flags from `AF_AGENT` defaults.
glossary._quiet_explicit: Sentinel key written to `ctx.obj` by the `--quiet`/`--verbose` option callback when the user explicitly passes either flag, used to distinguish explicit flags from `AF_AGENT` defaults.
glossary.af/json_io.py: Compatibility shim file that re-exports `emit`, `emit_line`, `emit_error`, and `read_stdin` from `agentfox/io/json.py`; removed in Spec 04.
glossary.afspec: Base package depended on by both `agentfox` and `agentspec` in the monorepo dependency graph.
glossary.agentfox/io/: The new unified terminal I/O Python package created by this spec, located at `agentfox/io/` within the monorepo.
glossary.agentspec: Sibling Python package in the monorepo providing `AgentError`, `AgentSpecError`, and `SessionError`; lazily imported by `agentfox/io/errors.py`.
glossary.cli_error_handler: Function in `agentfox/io/errors.py` that routes an exception to either JSON stdout or plain-text stderr based on the active `json_mode`.
glossary.common_options: A Click decorator defined in `agentfox/io/cli.py` that adds `--verbose`, `--quiet`, `--trace`, and `--json`/`--no-json` flags to the root Click group.
glossary.ctx.obj: Click's context object dictionary used to pass data between the root group and subcommands; `OutputManager` is stored under the key `"output"`.
glossary.detail: Optional field in the error envelope `error` object, present only for `internal_error` type, containing the exception class name to aid debugging.
glossary.emit: Function in `agentfox/io/json.py` that writes pretty-printed JSON (indent=2) to stdout.
glossary.emit_error: Function in `agentfox/io/json.py` that always writes a structured JSON error envelope to stdout regardless of json_mode.
glossary.emit_line: Function in `agentfox/io/json.py` that writes compact JSONL (no indentation) to stdout.
glossary.emit_ok: Function in `agentfox/io/json.py` that writes a JSON object with `"ok": true` merged with caller-supplied data to stdout.
glossary.error_envelope: Function in `agentfox/io/errors.py` that builds a structured error dict `{"ok": false, "error": {...}}` from any exception without serializing or printing it.
glossary.exit_codes: Decorator from `agentfox/io/help.py` that stores an exit-code-to-description mapping as an attribute on a Click Command object.
glossary.get_output_manager: Convenience function in `agentfox/io/output.py` that returns the active `OutputManager` from the current Click context, or a fallback instance if no context is active.
glossary.handle_cli_errors: No-argument decorator in `agentfox/io/errors.py` that wraps command functions to catch exceptions and delegate to `cli_error_handler`.
glossary.internal_error: The catch-all error type string assigned to exceptions not matched by more specific type mappings; always accompanied by a `detail` field containing the exception class name.
glossary.json_mode: Boolean field on `OutputManager` controlling whether output is written as JSON to stdout (`True`) or as human-readable text (`False`).
glossary.quiet: Boolean field on `OutputManager`; when `True`, suppresses banner and status lines on stderr.
glossary.read_stdin: Function in `agentfox/io/json.py` that reads and parses a JSON object from piped stdin, returning `{}` for interactive TTY or empty input.
glossary.setup_logging: Existing function in `agentfox/core/logging.py` that configures the root logger level based on verbose, quiet, and trace flags.
glossary.state: Optional free-form string parameter passed to `emit_error` and `error_envelope` representing the workflow phase (e.g. `"planning"`, `"executing"`) when an error occurred.

requirements.title: agentfox/io/ package structure and public API

user_story.goal: import any of the twelve curated public symbols directly from `agentfox.io`
user_story.benefit: I have a single, stable import surface without needing to know internal submodule locations

acceptance_criteria.action: re-exports exactly the twelve public symbols: `OutputManager`, `StatusSpinner`, `get_output_manager`, `emit`, `emit_ok`, `emit_line`, `emit_error`, `read_stdin`, `error_envelope`, `AgentFoxGroup`, `common_options`, `exit_codes`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: All twelve symbols are importable via `from agentfox.io import <symbol>`; no additional symbols beyond these twelve are exposed at the package level

acceptance_criteria.action: does not re-export `handle_cli_errors`; that symbol is available only via `from agentfox.io.errors import handle_cli_errors`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `from agentfox.io import handle_cli_errors` raises `ImportError`; `from agentfox.io.errors import handle_cli_errors` succeeds

acceptance_criteria.action: consists of exactly the seven files: `__init__.py`, `output.py`, `json.py`, `spinner.py`, `errors.py`, `cli.py`, `help.py`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: All seven files exist at the specified paths within the `agentfox/io/` directory

edge_cases.action: raises `ImportError` for the unlisted symbol; the consumer must import from the specific submodule instead
edge_cases.return_contract: `ImportError` is raised with a message indicating the symbol is not available at the package level
edge_cases.error_condition: a consumer attempts to import a submodule-internal symbol (e.g. `handle_cli_errors`) directly from `agentfox.io`

user_story.goal: retrieve a pre-constructed `OutputManager` from `ctx.obj["output"]` without constructing one myself
user_story.benefit: I can focus on command logic rather than output mode resolution

acceptance_criteria.action: holds fields `json_mode: bool`, `quiet: bool`, `verbose: bool`, `trace: bool`, and `console: Console` (Rich console for stderr)
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: All five fields are accessible on every `OutputManager` instance

acceptance_criteria.action: calls `ctx.ensure_object(dict)`, reads sentinel keys to resolve flags, constructs an `OutputManager`, and stores it at `ctx.obj["output"]`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `ctx.obj["output"]` is a fully constructed `OutputManager` instance before any subcommand executes

acceptance_criteria.action: returns the `OutputManager` from `ctx.obj["output"]` of the current Click context; when no Click context is active, returns a fallback `OutputManager` with `json_mode=False`, `quiet=False`, `verbose=False`, `trace=False`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Returns a valid `OutputManager` in both cases; `AF_AGENT` env var is NOT consulted in the fallback path

acceptance_criteria.action: logs a debug-level warning and falls back to constructing `OutputManager` with defaults (honoring `AF_AGENT` env var but with no sentinel data)
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: A default `OutputManager` is constructed and the CLI does not crash; a debug-level warning is emitted to the logger
acceptance_criteria.state: `ctx.obj` is already set to a non-dict value by an upstream parent group

edge_cases.action: returns the fallback `OutputManager` with `json_mode=False` — `AF_AGENT` is not consulted in the fallback path
edge_cases.return_contract: Fallback `OutputManager` has `json_mode=False`, `quiet=False`, `verbose=False`, `trace=False` regardless of `AF_AGENT` environment variable
edge_cases.error_condition: no Click context is active (e.g. called from a test or library context) and `AF_AGENT` is set to `"1"` in the environment

user_story.goal: set `AF_AGENT=1` once in my environment to enable JSON output and quiet mode for all CLI invocations
user_story.benefit: I do not need to pass `--json --quiet` on every command invocation

acceptance_criteria.action: defaults `json_mode=True` and `quiet=True` when constructing the `OutputManager`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `OutputManager` has `json_mode=True` and `quiet=True`
acceptance_criteria.state: `AF_AGENT` environment variable is set to exactly the string `"1"` and no explicit format flags are passed

acceptance_criteria.action: sets `json_mode=False` (explicit flag overrides env default) while `quiet` remains `True`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `OutputManager` has `json_mode=False` and `quiet=True`

acceptance_criteria.action: sets `quiet=False` (explicit flag overrides env default) while `json_mode` remains `True`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `OutputManager` has `json_mode=True` and `quiet=False`

acceptance_criteria.action: sets `json_mode=False` and `quiet=False`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `OutputManager` has `json_mode=False` and `quiet=False`

acceptance_criteria.action: treats `AF_AGENT` values other than exactly `"1"` (e.g. `"true"`, `"yes"`, `"on"`, `"0"`, empty string) as if `AF_AGENT` is unset — agent mode is not activated
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Only `AF_AGENT=1` (exact string) activates agent mode; all other values leave default behavior unchanged

acceptance_criteria.action: implements `--json`/`--no-json` using a Click option pair with a callback that calls `ctx.ensure_object(dict)` then sets `ctx.obj["_json_explicit"] = True` when either flag is explicitly passed; the `--quiet`/`--verbose` callback sets `ctx.obj["_quiet_explicit"] = True` when either flag is explicitly passed
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `ctx.obj["_json_explicit"]` is `True` iff the user passed `--json` or `--no-json`; `ctx.obj["_quiet_explicit"]` is `True` iff the user passed `--quiet` or `--verbose`

edge_cases.action: does not activate agent mode; `json_mode` and `quiet` use their normal defaults (`False`)
edge_cases.return_contract: `OutputManager` has `json_mode=False` and `quiet=False` (or whatever explicit flags dictate)
edge_cases.error_condition: `AF_AGENT` is set to `"true"`, `"yes"`, `"on"`, `"0"`, or empty string

user_story.goal: use a single `OutputManager` instance to dispatch output to either JSON or human-readable format
user_story.benefit: I do not need to repeat `if json_mode: ... else: ...` in every command

acceptance_criteria.action: writes the dict serialized as pretty-printed JSON (indent=2) to stdout
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: JSON string with 2-space indentation is written to stdout

acceptance_criteria.action: silently no-ops; nothing is written to stdout
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: No output is produced

acceptance_criteria.action: writes the plain text string to stdout
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Plain text string is written to stdout

acceptance_criteria.action: silently no-ops; nothing is written to stdout
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: No output is produced

acceptance_criteria.action: calls `emit_json(data)` to write pretty-printed JSON to stdout; `human_fn` is ignored
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: JSON output is written to stdout; `human_fn` is not called

acceptance_criteria.action: calls `human_fn()` to produce human-readable output; no JSON is written
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `human_fn()` is called exactly once; no JSON output is written to stdout

acceptance_criteria.action: silently no-ops; no output is produced
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: No output is produced

acceptance_criteria.action: renders the themed banner on stderr; suppressed when `json_mode=True` or `quiet=True`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Banner is written to stderr only when both `json_mode=False` and `quiet=False`

acceptance_criteria.action: writes the message to stderr; suppressed when `quiet=True`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Message is written to stderr only when `quiet=False`

user_story.benefit: I get consistent JSON output format and error envelopes without writing custom serialization code

acceptance_criteria.action: writes the dict to stdout as pretty-printed JSON using `indent=2` and `default=str` for non-serializable values
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Valid JSON string with 2-space indentation written to stdout; non-serializable values (e.g. `datetime`, `UUID`, `Path`) are coerced via `str()`

acceptance_criteria.action: writes the dict to stdout as compact JSON (no indentation) on a single line, using `default=str`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Compact JSON string with no indentation written to stdout followed by a newline

acceptance_criteria.action: merges `{"ok": True}` into the caller-supplied dict (always overwriting the `"ok"` key) and writes as pretty-printed JSON with `indent=2` to stdout
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: JSON object with `"ok": true` at top level written to stdout; caller-supplied `"ok"` key is silently overwritten

acceptance_criteria.action: always writes a structured JSON error envelope to stdout regardless of `json_mode`; calls `error_envelope(exc, state=state)` internally to build the dict, then serializes and prints
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: JSON object conforming to `{"ok": false, "error": {"type": ..., "message": ..., "retryable": ...}}` written to stdout; `"state"` top-level field included iff `state` is non-`None`

acceptance_criteria.action: reads from stdin assuming UTF-8 encoding; returns `{}` if stdin is an interactive TTY or is empty; returns parsed dict if stdin contains valid UTF-8 JSON; blocks until EOF for piped stdin with no timeout
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Returns `dict`; returns `{}` for interactive TTY or empty input

acceptance_criteria.action: silently suppresses `BrokenPipeError` by wrapping the stdout write in `try/except BrokenPipeError: pass`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: No exception is raised or propagated to the caller when the downstream pipe is closed

edge_cases.action: overwrites the caller's `"ok"` value with `True`; no warning is emitted
edge_cases.return_contract: Emitted JSON contains `"ok": true` regardless of the input dict's `"ok"` field

edge_cases.error_condition: stdin contains malformed JSON (valid UTF-8 but not parseable)

user_story.role: AI coding agent calling both `af` and `spec` CLIs
user_story.goal: receive a consistent structured error envelope from both CLIs whenever an error occurs
user_story.benefit: I can parse and handle errors from both CLIs using a single schema without conditional logic

acceptance_criteria.action: builds and returns a structured dict `{"ok": False, "error": {"type": ..., "message": ..., "retryable": ...}}` from any exception; does not serialize or print
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Returns a `dict` with `"ok": False` and an `"error"` sub-dict containing non-empty string `"type"`, non-empty string `"message"` (from `str(exc)`), and boolean `"retryable"`

acceptance_criteria.action: derives `"type"` from `AgentFoxError` subclasses by converting the class name to snake_case at runtime (e.g. `ConfigError` → `"config_error"`); applies to all `AgentFoxError` subclasses including unknown custom ones
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `"type"` field is the snake_case form of the exception class name; `"retryable"` is the per-class attribute value

acceptance_criteria.action: for `AgentError` with `.category`: sets `"type"` to `.category` value; for `AgentError` without `.category`: sets `"type"` to `"agent_error"` and `"retryable"` to `False`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `"type"` is `.category` if present, else `"agent_error"`; `"retryable"` is per-instance attribute if present, else `False`

acceptance_criteria.action: for `SessionError`: sets `"type"` to `"session_error"` and `"retryable"` to `False` regardless of any instance attributes
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `"type": "session_error"` and `"retryable": false` always for `SessionError`

acceptance_criteria.action: for `click.ClickException`: sets `"type"` to `"input_error"` and `"retryable"` to `False`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `"type": "input_error"` and `"retryable": false` for all `click.ClickException` instances

acceptance_criteria.action: for all other/unknown exceptions: sets `"type"` to `"internal_error"`, `"retryable"` to `False`, and includes a `"detail"` field with the exception class name; `"detail"` is omitted for well-typed exceptions
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `"type": "internal_error"`, `"retryable": false`, and `"error.detail": "<ClassName>"` for unknown exceptions; `"detail"` key absent for `AgentFoxError`, `AgentError`, `AgentSpecError`, `SessionError`, and `click.ClickException`

acceptance_criteria.action: includes `"state"` as a top-level field in the returned dict when `state` is non-`None`; omits `"state"` entirely when `state` is `None`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Top-level `"state"` key present iff `state` argument is non-`None`

acceptance_criteria.action: lazily imports `AgentError`, `AgentSpecError`, `SessionError` from `agentspec` using `try/except ImportError`; gracefully skips agentspec type mapping when the package is not installed
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: When `agentspec` is not installed, agentspec exception instances fall through to `internal_error` mapping; no `ImportError` is raised at module load time

edge_cases.action: exception falls through to `internal_error` mapping; `"type": "internal_error"`, `"retryable": false`, `"detail"` set to class name
edge_cases.return_contract: Valid error envelope with `"type": "internal_error"` and `"detail"` field; no `ImportError` raised
edge_cases.error_condition: agentspec is not installed and an `AgentError`/`AgentSpecError`/`SessionError` instance is passed

user_story.goal: have errors automatically routed to JSON stdout or plain-text stderr based on the current output mode
user_story.benefit: I do not need to manually check `json_mode` in error-handling code

acceptance_criteria.action: calls `emit_error(exc)` to write structured JSON envelope to stdout
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Structured JSON error envelope written to stdout; nothing written to stderr for the error

acceptance_criteria.action: calls `click.echo(str(exc), err=True)` to write plain text to stderr
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Plain text error message written to stderr; nothing written to stdout

acceptance_criteria.action: takes no arguments (applied as `@handle_cli_errors` without parentheses); wraps the decorated function; when the function raises an `Exception` (not `SystemExit` or `KeyboardInterrupt`), resolves `json_mode` dynamically via `get_output_manager()` at call time and delegates to `cli_error_handler()`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `json_mode` is resolved at call time (not decoration time); `SystemExit` and `KeyboardInterrupt` propagate without being caught

acceptance_criteria.action: catches `Exception` subclasses (not `BaseException`), routes through `cli_error_handler`, then calls `sys.exit(1)`; re-raises `SystemExit` and `KeyboardInterrupt` immediately without routing
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Exit code 1 for all caught `Exception` subclasses; exit code 0 on success; `SystemExit` and `KeyboardInterrupt` propagate normally

edge_cases.action: re-raises `SystemExit` immediately without routing through `cli_error_handler` or calling `sys.exit(1)`
edge_cases.return_contract: Process exits with the original `SystemExit` code; no error envelope is emitted
`KeyboardInterrupt` propagates normally; no error envelope is emitted; no `sys.exit(1)` is called by the group

user_story.role: CLI developer needing animated progress feedback
user_story.goal: use a single `StatusSpinner` class for all progress display needs
user_story.benefit: there is no duplicated spinner logic and the behavior is consistent across both `af` and `spec` CLIs

acceptance_criteria.action: is a context manager (`__enter__`/`__exit__`) that accepts `message: str`, `quiet: bool = False`, and `theme: AppTheme | None = None`; provides `update(message: str)` and `log(message: str)` methods
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: All four methods exist and are callable on every `StatusSpinner` instance

acceptance_criteria.action: displays an animated Rich spinner using the `"dots"` style on stderr in animated mode; `update()` changes the spinner message; `log()` prints a persistent line through Rich `Live`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Animated `"dots"` spinner displayed on stderr; `update()` changes the displayed message; `log()` appends a persistent line

acceptance_criteria.action: prints plain text lines to stderr for both `update()` and `log()` calls instead of animating; uses `theme.console.print(message)` when `theme` is provided, or fallback `Console(stderr=True).print(message)` when `theme=None`; no additional markup applied by `StatusSpinner`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Plain text lines written to stderr for each `update()` and `log()` call; no Rich animation
acceptance_criteria.state: stdout/stderr is not a TTY and `quiet=False`

acceptance_criteria.action: all methods (`update()`, `log()`, `__enter__()`, `__exit__()`) are no-ops; no output is produced
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: No output to stdout or stderr in quiet mode

acceptance_criteria.action: uses Rich `Live` internally; concurrent `update()` and `log()` calls are serialized by Rich `Live`'s internal lock; `__exit__` must be called from the same thread as `__enter__`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: No race conditions between `update()` and `log()` calls from the same thread; cross-thread `__exit__` is unsupported

acceptance_criteria.action: replaces both the legacy `PlanSpinner` in `agentfox/ui/progress.py` and the legacy `StatusSpinner` in `spec/ui.py`; no duplicated spinner logic remains after migration
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Exactly one `StatusSpinner` class exists in the codebase at `agentfox/io/spinner.py`; legacy spinner classes are removed or delegate to it

edge_cases.action: falls back to a `Rich Console(stderr=True)` with no styling for all output including `log()` and non-TTY `update()` messages
edge_cases.return_contract: Output is produced on stderr with no custom styling; no `AttributeError` or `TypeError` raised

requirements.title: common_options decorator and root-group flag scope

user_story.role: CLI developer adding common flags to a root Click group
user_story.goal: apply `common_options` once to the root group and have subcommands automatically inherit resolved settings
user_story.benefit: I avoid duplicate flag registration on subcommands and get a clear error if I misuse the decorator

acceptance_criteria.action: adds `--verbose`, `--quiet`, `--trace`, and `--json`/`--no-json` flags to the decorated root Click group; subcommands do not re-declare these flags and instead receive the resolved `OutputManager` via `ctx.obj["output"]`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: All four flag groups are registered on the root group; subcommands have no duplicate flags

acceptance_criteria.action: raises `TypeError` at decoration time with a descriptive message
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `TypeError` raised immediately at decoration time with message such as `"common_options must be applied to the root Click group, not to a subcommand"`
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: accidentally applied to a Click `Command` that is not a `Group` (i.e. a subcommand)

acceptance_criteria.action: skips registering the conflicting flag and emits a debug-level warning to the logger; the root group's existing flag takes precedence
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: No duplicate flag registered; debug-level warning logged; no exception raised
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a name collision is detected between a common flag and an existing flag on the root group

requirements.title: exit_codes decorator for Click command metadata

user_story.role: CLI developer documenting exit codes for a command
user_story.goal: annotate my Click command with `@exit_codes` to store exit code metadata for future structured help rendering
user_story.benefit: exit code mappings are stored on the Command object and ready for Spec 04's help renderer without requiring changes to decorated commands

acceptance_criteria.action: is written above `@click.command`; receives the already-constructed Click `Command` object and sets `command.exit_codes` to the provided mapping dict
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `command.exit_codes` attribute is set to the provided mapping dict; the `Command` object is returned unchanged otherwise

acceptance_criteria.action: raises `TypeError` with a descriptive message (e.g. `"@exit_codes must be applied above @click.command; received a plain function, not a Click Command"`)
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `TypeError` raised immediately at decoration time with descriptive message
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: applied below `@click.command` in source (receives a raw Python function instead of a Click `Command`)

acceptance_criteria.action: the second application overwrites `command.exit_codes` with the new mapping; no merge is performed and no warning is emitted
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `command.exit_codes` contains only the mapping from the second (outermost) `@exit_codes` application
acceptance_criteria.trigger: applied twice to the same command

acceptance_criteria.action: defers all structured JSON help rendering to Spec 04; `--help` behavior is unchanged from Click's standard formatted text help in this spec
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `--help` output is Click's standard human-readable text in all cases; no JSON help rendering occurs in Spec 03

user_story.goal: have `af/app.py` use `AgentFoxGroup` as the root Click group class
user_story.benefit: `af` gains unified banner rendering, error handling, and `OutputManager` support without maintaining a separate `BannerGroup` implementation

acceptance_criteria.action: replaces the existing root group class (e.g. `BannerGroup`) with `cls=AgentFoxGroup`; `AgentFoxGroup` subsumes all banner rendering, error handling, and `OutputManager` construction behavior previously provided by the existing group class
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `af` CLI uses `AgentFoxGroup` as root group; no separate `BannerGroup` class remains active

acceptance_criteria.action: includes an inline comment block at the `BannerGroup` → `AgentFoxGroup` replacement site documenting: behaviors confirmed as covered by `AgentFoxGroup`, behaviors explicitly deferred to Spec 04, and the date of the audit
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Inline comment block is present in `af/app.py` at the replacement site as evidence of the pre-migration audit

acceptance_criteria.action: continues to use `click.echo()` directly and does not call `get_output_manager()` or reference `ctx.obj` before `OutputManager` is constructed
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `af --version` outputs the version string and exits without error; no `KeyError` or `AttributeError` raised

user_story.goal: have my existing `from af.json_io import emit, emit_line, emit_error, read_stdin` imports continue to work unchanged after the migration
user_story.benefit: I can migrate incrementally in Spec 04 without urgent breaking changes in Spec 03

acceptance_criteria.action: re-exports exactly four symbols from `agentfox/io/json.py`: `emit`, `emit_line`, `emit_error`, `read_stdin`; no other symbols are re-exported; `emit_ok` and `error_envelope` are intentionally excluded
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `from af.json_io import emit, emit_line, emit_error, read_stdin` succeeds; `from af.json_io import emit_ok` raises `ImportError`

acceptance_criteria.action: is explicitly marked as a temporary compatibility shim with a comment indicating removal in Spec 04
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Comment `# compatibility shim, removed in Spec 04` (or equivalent) is present in the file

user_story.goal: have the `spec` CLI behave identically before and after Spec 03 lands
user_story.benefit: I am not exposed to any regressions from the `agentfox/io/` migration until Spec 05 deliberately migrates `spec`

acceptance_criteria.action: is not modified in Spec 03; all inline JSON/error patterns in `spec/cli.py` remain entirely unchanged; no compatibility shim is introduced for `spec`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `spec/cli.py` is byte-for-byte identical before and after Spec 03 is applied; all existing `spec` CLI tests pass unchanged

requirements.title: No regressions in existing test suites

user_story.goal: have all pre-existing `af` and `spec` CLI unit and integration tests pass without modification after the migration
user_story.benefit: the existing test suite serves as the regression contract and no test discipline is weakened

acceptance_criteria.action: runs all pre-existing `af` and `spec` CLI unit tests and integration tests against the migrated code without modification; all tests pass
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: Zero test failures; zero tests deleted, skipped, or marked `xfail` to satisfy this requirement

acceptance_criteria.action: each of the seven new modules ships with dedicated unit tests covering happy-path behavior, error/exception handling, quiet-mode no-ops, non-TTY fallback, `AF_AGENT=1` precedence, edge cases enumerated in this spec, and the specific behaviors listed in the Testing Strategy
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: All new unit tests pass in CI

acceptance_criteria.action: property tests verify that any `AgentFoxError`, `AgentError`, `AgentSpecError`, `SessionError`, or `click.ClickException` can be serialized to a valid unified error envelope where: `type` is a non-empty string, `message` is a non-empty string from `str(exc)`, `retryable` is a boolean, `detail` is present iff the exception falls to `internal_error`, `state` is present iff non-`None` was passed, and `emit_error()` output is valid JSON matching `error_envelope()` for the same inputs
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: All Hypothesis property tests pass; agentspec-dependent property tests are guarded with `pytest.importorskip("agentspec")` and skipped when agentspec is not installed

user_story.role: CLI developer relying on log-level configuration
user_story.goal: have `setup_logging` called automatically with the correct resolved flags when the CLI starts
user_story.benefit: I do not need to manually call `setup_logging` in each command or worry about log-level misconfiguration

acceptance_criteria.action: calls `setup_logging(verbose=<resolved>, quiet=<resolved>, trace=<resolved>)` with the flag values derived from sentinels and `AF_AGENT` defaults
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: `setup_logging()` is called exactly once per CLI invocation with the correct `verbose`, `quiet`, and `trace` values
acceptance_criteria.trigger: the group's invoke method runs after resolving flags

correctness_properties.title: Error envelope always valid
correctness_properties.for_any: exception `exc` of any type passed to `error_envelope(exc)`
correctness_properties.invariant: `error_envelope(exc)` returns a dict where `"ok"` is `False`, `"error.type"` is a non-empty string, `"error.message"` equals `str(exc)` and is non-empty, `"error.retryable"` is a boolean, and `"error.detail"` is present if and only if the exception maps to `internal_error`

correctness_properties.title: emit_error output is valid JSON matching error_envelope
correctness_properties.invariant: `emit_error(exc, state=state)` writes output parseable by `json.loads()` whose structure equals `error_envelope(exc, state=state)` for the same inputs; `emit_error()` always writes to stdout regardless of `json_mode`

correctness_properties.title: AF_AGENT precedence: explicit flags always win
correctness_properties.for_any: combination of `AF_AGENT` environment value and explicit CLI flags `--json`/`--no-json`/`--quiet`/`--verbose`
correctness_properties.invariant: when `_json_explicit` sentinel is set, the explicit flag value for `json_mode` always takes precedence over `AF_AGENT=1` default; when `_quiet_explicit` sentinel is set, the explicit flag value for `quiet` always takes precedence over `AF_AGENT=1` default

correctness_properties.title: emit_ok always sets ok to true
correctness_properties.for_any: dict `data` passed to `emit_ok(data)` including dicts where `data["ok"] = False`
correctness_properties.invariant: the JSON written to stdout always contains `"ok": true` at the top level regardless of any `"ok"` key in the input `data`

correctness_properties.title: BrokenPipeError always suppressed in emit functions
correctness_properties.for_any: invocation of `emit()`, `emit_line()`, `emit_ok()`, or `emit_error()` when stdout pipe is closed
correctness_properties.invariant: no `BrokenPipeError` propagates to the caller; all four emit functions complete without raising an exception when stdout is closed

correctness_properties.title: AgentFoxError subclasses always produce snake_case type
correctness_properties.for_any: `AgentFoxError` subclass instance `exc` including dynamically created unknown subclasses
correctness_properties.invariant: `error_envelope(exc)["error"]["type"]` equals the snake_case form of `type(exc).__name__`; no `AgentFoxError` subclass falls through to `internal_error`

correctness_properties.title: OutputManager format dispatch mutual exclusion
correctness_properties.for_any: `OutputManager` instance with any combination of `json_mode` and `quiet` flags
correctness_properties.invariant: `emit_json()` writes to stdout iff `json_mode=True`; `emit_human()` writes to stdout iff `json_mode=False`; `banner()` writes to stderr iff `json_mode=False` and `quiet=False`; these behaviors are mutually exclusive with their no-op conditions

correctness_properties.title: get_output_manager fallback ignores AF_AGENT
correctness_properties.for_any: any environment where `AF_AGENT` may or may not be set
correctness_properties.invariant: when no Click context is active, `get_output_manager()` always returns an `OutputManager` with `json_mode=False`, `quiet=False`, `verbose=False`, `trace=False` — the `AF_AGENT` env var is never consulted in the fallback path

steps.action: sets `AF_AGENT=1` in the environment and invokes the `af` CLI without passing any format flags
calls `ctx.ensure_object(dict)`, reads sentinels — finds `_json_explicit` and `_quiet_explicit` absent — and checks `AF_AGENT` env var; finds exactly `"1"`, sets `json_mode=True` and `quiet=True`
constructs `OutputManager(json_mode=True, quiet=True, ...)` and stores it at `ctx.obj["output"]`; calls `setup_logging(verbose=False, quiet=True, trace=False)`
skips banner rendering because `json_mode=True`
retrieves `OutputManager` via `ctx.obj["output"]` or `get_output_manager()` and executes; calls `emit_ok({"result": ...})` to produce JSON output to stdout
receives pretty-printed JSON response `{"ok": true, "result": ...}` with `indent=2`

execution_paths.title: Error in JSON mode producing structured envelope

steps.action: invokes `af <command>` with `--json` flag or `AF_AGENT=1`
constructs `OutputManager(json_mode=True, ...)` and stores it at `ctx.obj["output"]`
raises an `AgentFoxError` subclass (e.g. `ConfigError`) during execution
catches the `Exception`; calls `cli_error_handler(ctx, exc)`

reads `json_mode=True` from `OutputManager`; calls `emit_error(exc)` which internally calls `error_envelope(exc)` to build `{"ok": false, "error": {"type": "config_error", "message": "...", "retryable": false}}`
receives the structured JSON error envelope
calls `sys.exit(1)` after `cli_error_handler` returns

execution_paths.title: Error in human mode producing plain-text stderr message

steps.action: invokes `af <command>` without any format flags and without `AF_AGENT=1`
constructs `OutputManager(json_mode=False, quiet=False, ...)` and stores it at `ctx.obj["output"]`; renders banner to stderr
raises an exception during execution
catches the `Exception`; calls `cli_error_handler(ctx, exc)`
reads `json_mode=False` from `OutputManager`; calls `click.echo(str(exc), err=True)` to write plain text to stderr
receives the plain-text error message
calls `sys.exit(1)` after `cli_error_handler` returns
creates `StatusSpinner(message="Processing...", quiet=False, theme=None)` and enters the context manager
detects that stderr is not a TTY; initializes fallback `Console(stderr=True)` since `theme=None`; does not start Rich Live animation
calls `spinner.update("Step 1 complete")` during processing
prints `"Step 1 complete"` as a plain text line to stderr via fallback `Console(stderr=True).print(message)`
calls `spinner.log("Detail logged")` to emit a persistent log line
prints `"Detail logged"` as a plain text line to stderr via fallback `Console(stderr=True).print(message)`
exits the context manager via `StatusSpinner.__exit__()`
has received two plain-text lines: `"Step 1 complete"` and `"Detail logged"`
sets `AF_AGENT=1` in the environment and invokes `af <command> --no-json`
calls `ctx.ensure_object(dict)` then sets `ctx.obj["_json_explicit"] = True` and stores the flag value `False`
reads `ctx.obj["_json_explicit"] = True`; uses explicit flag value `json_mode=False`; `AF_AGENT=1` env default for json_mode is ignored
reads `_quiet_explicit` absent; applies `AF_AGENT=1` quiet default: `quiet=True`
constructs `OutputManager(json_mode=False, quiet=True, ...)`; banner is suppressed because `quiet=True`
runs and calls `OutputManager.emit_human(text)` which writes plain text to stdout (json_mode=False)
receives plain-text output
pipes a JSON object to `af <command>` via stdin (e.g. `echo '{"key": "val"}' | af plan`)
calls `read_stdin()` to consume piped input
detects stdin is not an interactive TTY; reads from stdin until EOF using UTF-8 encoding; parses JSON
returns the parsed dict `{"key": "val"}`
uses the parsed dict as input parameters for the command logic
invokes `af --version`
processes the eager `--version` option before `AgentFoxGroup.invoke()` completes
calls `click.echo(<version_string>)` directly to stdout; does not call `get_output_manager()` or access `ctx.obj`
raises `SystemExit(0)` to terminate the process
does not catch `SystemExit`; it propagates normally
exits with code 0; version string was written to stdout
catches an exception during the `"executing"` workflow phase and calls `emit_error(exc, state="executing")`
calls `error_envelope(exc, state="executing")` to build the structured dict
builds `{"ok": false, "state": "executing", "error": {"type": "agent_error", "message": "...", "retryable": true}}`
serializes the dict to JSON and writes to stdout regardless of current `json_mode`
receives the full JSON envelope including the top-level `"state": "executing"` field

error_handling.condition: `BrokenPipeError` raised when writing to stdout in any emit function
error_handling.behavior: Silently suppressed via `try/except BrokenPipeError: pass`; no exception propagates to the caller; no error envelope is emitted

error_handling.condition: `read_stdin()` receives malformed JSON (valid UTF-8 but not parseable)
error_handling.behavior: `json.JSONDecodeError` is raised and propagates to the caller without being caught
`UnicodeDecodeError` is raised and propagates to the caller without being caught

error_handling.condition: An `Exception` subclass is raised during `AgentFoxGroup.invoke()` execution of a subcommand
error_handling.behavior: Exception is caught by `AgentFoxGroup`; `cli_error_handler` routes to JSON stdout or plain-text stderr based on `json_mode`; `sys.exit(1)` is called; the exception is not re-raised

error_handling.condition: `SystemExit` is raised during CLI execution (e.g. from `--help`, `--version`, or explicit `sys.exit(0)`)
error_handling.behavior: `SystemExit` is re-raised immediately by `AgentFoxGroup` without routing through `cli_error_handler`; process exits with the original exit code
`KeyboardInterrupt` is re-raised immediately by `AgentFoxGroup` without routing through `cli_error_handler`; no error envelope is emitted

error_handling.condition: `agentspec` is not installed and an `AgentError`, `AgentSpecError`, or `SessionError` instance reaches `error_envelope()`
error_handling.behavior: Exception falls through to `internal_error` mapping; envelope contains `"type": "internal_error"`, `"retryable": false`, and `"detail": "<ClassName>"`; no `ImportError` is raised

error_handling.condition: `common_options` decorator is applied to a Click `Command` that is not a `Group` (a subcommand)
error_handling.behavior: `TypeError` is raised at decoration time with a descriptive message; the subcommand is not registered

error_handling.condition: `@exit_codes` decorator receives a raw Python function instead of a Click `Command` object (applied in wrong order relative to `@click.command`)
error_handling.behavior: `TypeError` is raised immediately at decoration time with a descriptive message such as `"@exit_codes must be applied above @click.command; received a plain function, not a Click Command"`

error_handling.condition: `ctx.obj` is already set to a non-dict value by an upstream parent group when `AgentFoxGroup.invoke()` runs
error_handling.behavior: `AgentFoxGroup` logs a debug-level warning and falls back to constructing `OutputManager` with defaults honoring `AF_AGENT` env var but no sentinel data; CLI execution continues without crashing

error_handling.condition: An eager option callback (e.g. `--version`) fires before `AgentFoxGroup.invoke()` completes and `ctx.obj["output"]` is not yet populated
error_handling.behavior: Eager option callbacks use `click.echo()` directly and do not call `get_output_manager()`; no `KeyError` or `AttributeError` is raised

error_handling.condition: An unknown/unmapped exception type (not `AgentFoxError`, `AgentError`, `AgentSpecError`, `SessionError`, or `click.ClickException`) is passed to `error_envelope()`
error_handling.behavior: Envelope is built with `"type": "internal_error"`, `"retryable": false`, and `"error.detail": "<ClassName>"` containing the exception class name; no exception is raised by `error_envelope()` itself
